summary: The root فتأ (ftA) in its fourth form (أَفْتَاَ) refers back to earlier definitions. It implies a sense of weakness, languor, or becoming feeble, often in health or spirit.
lane: 4 أَفْتَاَ see the preceding paragraph, in two places.

headwords.def: مَا فَتِئَ, (Fr, * T, Msb, K,) aor. فَتَاَ, (Fr, T, Msb;) and ما فَتَأَ, [aor. فَتَاَ;] (K;) and ما فَتُؤَ, (Fr, * T, K,) aor. فَتُاَ; (Fr, T;) He did not cease [doing a thing; being incomplete, or non-attributive, verbs]; (T, Msb, K;) as also مَا; (AZ, T, K;) this last of the dial. of Temeem; (AZ, T, M;) the first of the dial. of Keys and others: (AZ, T:) you say مَا فَتِئْتُ أَ ْكُرُهُ, (AZ, T, S, O, Msb, *) or مَا فَتِئْتُ أَفْعَلُ, (M,) and ما فَتَأْتُ, (AZ, T, S, O, M,) aor. فَتَاَ, inf.
أَفْتَاَ see the preceding paragraph, in two places.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
